surveys.what: Spartel palaeo-island proposed as Plato's Atlantis
surveys.method: Reading Plato against a map of the sunken bank, with a sea-level fall of about 100 m at the last glacial maximum.
surveys.finding: Proposed that an island in front of the Strait, now Spartel Bank, was drowned by the end-glacial sea-level rise.
surveys.evidence: 'Une ile faisant face au Detroit de Gibraltar et une geographie proche de celle evoquee par Platon dans le Timee ont disparu, engloutis 9000 ans avant notre ere par une acceleration de la transgression finiglaciaire (Collina-Girard 2001).' (2002 follow-up article, CC BY)
surveys.data_available: The 2001 paper is Comptes Rendus de l'Academie des Sciences IIA, doi:10.1016/s1251-8050(01)01629-9 (abstract not read; behind Elsevier). The 2002 follow-up is open.

surveys.what: Spartel Bank hypothesis tested with new multibeam bathymetry
surveys.method: High-resolution bathymetric map of the bank, a review of the Gulf of Cadiz turbidite record and the 1755 tsunami.
surveys.finding: The bank was an island at about 11.6 ka and a great earthquake plus tsunami is possible in the Gulf of Cadiz; the paper then discusses whether people could have lived there.
surveys.evidence: 'The detailed morphology of Spartel paleoisland, as determined from recently acquired high-resolution bathymetric data, is reported here. The viability of human habitation on this paleoisland ca. 11.6 ka is discussed on the basis of a new bathymetric map.' (abstract, HAL record)
surveys.data_available: Not stated in the abstract. The paper is paywalled (Geology 33, doi:10.1130/G21597.1; OpenAlex lists no open copy).
surveys.notes: Abstract only. I could not read the methods, so I cannot say which cruise supplied the Spartel bathymetry. The SWIM list names the 2003 TV-GIB cruise from Gutscher's institute; that link is my inference, not a statement in the paper.

browser.note: Not a picture service. A ranged GET with Origin: null returned 206 with access-control-allow-origin *, content-range bytes 139830-161429/466699830. So a script or a browser can read any window with byte ranges.

licence.name: Public domain, with attribution
licence.attribution: GEBCO Bathymetric Compilation Group 2026 (2026). The GEBCO_2026 Grid - a continuous terrain model for oceans and land at 15 arc-second intervals. NERC EDS British Oceanographic Data Centre NOC. doi:10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa

global_layers.notes: Read a window of the TID without downloading a 467 MB tile. Each GeoTIFF is one 90 by 90 degree tile, 21,600 by 21,600 cells of 15 arc-seconds (1/240 degree), 8-bit, uncompressed, one row per strip. Row r starts at byte 139830 + r*21600 (first strip offset read from the TIFF tag 273). Row r = floor((north_edge - lat) * 240); column c = floor((lon - west_edge) * 240). Send 'Range: bytes=A-B' for the rows you need; the server answers 206. Tile names: gebco_2026_tid_n90.0_s0.0_w-90.0_e0.0_geotiff.tif and the other seven (n90/n0 by w-180/-90/0/90). Codes are in the table in this file's notes. I used exactly this to compute the 'measured_or_predicted' numbers for 20 boxes. GEBCO says the cells it fills from the Seabed 2030 regional grids are 'sparse grids, i.e. only grid cells that contain data were populated', blended with a remove-restore step, so 'measured' means a measurement fed the cell, not that the cell holds a single raw sounding. Source: https://www.gebco.net/data-products-gridded-bathymetry-data/gebco2026-grid (read).

handoffs.what: Gorringe Bank (36.55 N, 11.1 W; GMRT shallowest cell 41 m in my box) and the banks west of the Strait belong with the Spartel entry; the SWIM compilation covers them.
Kuhne's Donana proposal is in Antiquity Project Gallery 78(300), 2004; I saw the title only. The published replies and the Hinojos fieldwork need a lane that can read them.
Cuban sonar claim (Zelitsky and Weinzweig, 2001): site said to be off the Guanahacabibes Peninsula at about 650 to 800 m; no coordinates published. Press only.
The Nomikou 2016 Santorini survey used a 2015 cruise 'as part of a documentary production ATLANTIS FOUND'; how that production framed the result belongs in the expeditions record.
Bimini Road: Harrison 1971 (Nature 230, 287), Shinn 1977 'Atlantis Hoax?' (unpublished) and the University of Miami radiocarbon list of 1979 are the chain of tests; I could not read the dates myself.

Sathiamurthy and Voris 2006 (Sunda Shelf flooding from -116 m at 21 ka) and Fitch et al. 2005 (Dogger Bank submerged about 7,500 years ago) give regional drowning dates; EMODnet Geology has sea-level index points and palaeocoastlines as map layers.

not_verified: GEBCO WMS (wms.gebco.net, all years): every GetMap returns an XML error inside an image/png response today. I could not draw TID from GEBCO itself; I used the NOAA-hosted GEBCO 2024 TID instead.
Gutscher 2005 (Geology 33, 685-688): paywalled; only the abstract (HAL record) was read. I do not know which cruise supplied the Spartel bathymetry, or the data policy.
Collina-Girard 2001 (Comptes Rendus IIA): behind Elsevier; the idea is documented from his open 2002 follow-up (CC BY), not from the 2001 text.

SWIM compilation grid: the paper says the 250 m xyz file is in its supplementary material; I did not fetch that file or confirm its licence. The 2005 Diez et al. paper (coverage 34 to 38 N, 12.5 to 5.5 W, 100 m grids, 19 surveys) came through a search summary; its host (raco.cat, core.ac.uk) blocked scripts.

EMODnet Bathymetry and EMODnet Geology licence pages: the catalogue says EMODnet's terms give CC BY 4.0 for EMODnet products and the page returned 403 to scripts; I did not re-read it. Per-layer licences for EMODnet Geology were not read.

PNOA lidar point densities: only the Andalusian second-coverage figure (1.5 points per m2, July 2020 to May 2021) was read, on the REDIAM bulletin. IGN's pages for the first, second and third coverages did not give readable text to my script; the figures 0.5, 0.5 to 4 or 0.5 to 2, and 5 points per m2 came through search summaries and disagree for the second coverage. No flight dates for the Donana tiles were read.

Donana/Hinojos: I found no open lidar-only product specific to the marsh, no CSIC Hinojos project data, and no sediment-core data for the marsh. A search summary mentioned a 2001 lidar terrain model of the Donana Natural Park in REDIAM; I did not open that record.
Kuhne 2004 (Antiquity) and Rodriguez-Ramirez et al. 2018 (Guadalquivir estuary chapter): titles and bibliographic records only; text not read.

Santorini: the Kolumbo survey paper (Nomikou et al. 2012) was not read (title and a search summary only). Akrotiri excavation plans (Archaeological Society at Athens, INSTAP and others) were not searched beyond one query; I found no open data. Greek national lidar for Thera was not found.

Azores: the EMEPC (Portuguese extended continental shelf) WMS at geoportal.snimar.pt and IHPT's gridmar.hidrografico.pt portal came up in a search summary with terms that bar commercial use; neither was fetched. Lourenco et al. 1998 (bathymetric compilation of the Azores Plateau): title only. Download sizes of the IHPT Azores grids not checked.
Canaries and Madeira: no Canary or Madeiran regional lidar or bathymetry service (IDECanarias, Madeira government) was found or tested; the national PNOA layer was tested only at Tenerife.

Richat: no open lidar, and no open large-scale geological map, was found. FABDEM (University of Bristol) and the Copernicus licence text were not read (the Bristol page timed out); AW3D30 (JAXA) was not tested. Matton and Jebrak 2014 ages (85 +/- 5 and 99 +/- 5 Ma) came from a search summary; the 2005 paper's abstract was read.

Bimini: Allen Coral Atlas terms and tile URL not found or read; the 1979 University of Miami radiocarbon dates and the beachrock conclusion came from a search summary; the Shinn and McKusick 1980 Nature note and Shinn's 2004 Skeptical Inquirer article were not read. A search summary also said uranium-thorium dating is disputed; I did not read it.

Cuba: the claimed site has no published coordinates, so my search box (-85 to -84, 21.8 to 22.6) is a guess around the western tip, not a pin. Depths of 650 m (BBC-based) and 800 m (a Spanish-language article) differ; I read neither source.

Souss-Massa, Tunisian chotts, the Atlas, Pampa Aullagas: only the global layers (terrain, imagery, Macrostrat) were tested. I searched for no national geological maps or lidar there and found no surveys to report.

Cyprus: Sarmast's claims and the published replies are not in the sources I read; Robertson 1998 is title only. Sardinia, Malta, the Black Sea shelf, the Celtic Shelf: high-resolution grid names come from the EMODnet list; the organisation behind EDMO 3339, 850, 697, 239 was not looked up, and download sizes were not checked.
Sundaland: Indonesia's national bathymetry (BATNAS) and DEMNAS were not searched; Sathiamurthy and Voris is the only paper read.

Antarctica: BedMachine v3 download needs a NASA Earthdata login which I did not test; IBCSO v2 (Southern Ocean) was named on GEBCO's page but not fetched; no file inside Bedmap3's six was downloaded. I did not compute TID for the Southern Ocean.
Global sample: the 'share measured' numbers come from 400 sampled rows, not the full grid, and I did not find an official figure to compare.

GEBCO TID numbers per place use the 2026 grid; the NOAA picture uses 2024. A cell flagged 'combination of direct methods' (TID 17) can come from a gridded regional compilation, so it is not a count of individual soundings.
NOAA NCEI licence text: none in any service metadata; catalogue entries stay share_ok false until someone reads NOAA's data policy.
